thread:
Lee (Support): FYI incoming escalation from James at Acme. They're seeing a bunch of requests that target eu-west being routed to us-east during peak windows -> big added latency and intermittent 503s. sample req_id: req_0a1b2c. Can we triage? :warning:
James (Customer): yep, started around 07:12 UTC. Responses slower by ~350-500ms and some 503/502. We haven't changed anything on our side.
Tom (Oncall): tagging karina and anya. Do we have routing logs for that req_id? Also any recent changes to spillover thresholds?
Karina (SRE): grabbing logs now. quick summary: eu-west GPU pool at ~98% util, queue length ~112. fallback policy triggered when in-flight + queue > 85% capacity -> autospill to fallback region (us-east). Router logs for req_0a1b2c: 
```
[2026-03-16T07:12:34Z] router: decide_route req=req_0a1b2c origin=eu-west policy=region_fallback target=us-east reason=capacity_exhausted
[2026-03-16T07:12:34Z] router: proxy_request req=req_0a1b2c target=us-east auth_scope=eu-only
[2026-03-16T07:12:35Z] proxy: upstream_response status=503 body="overloaded"
```
Karina (SRE): note the router forwarded the request without validating token-region compatibility. That double-hit (cross-region auth mismatch) is showing up intermittently as 401/403 in other traces too.
Anya (Eng Runtime): this is likely the bug we discussed in the routing thread — when fallback is triggered we should check token scope/pinned-region header and either reject early (429/403) or pick a compatible model variant, not blindly forward. I'll repro locally with the same token footprint.
Maria (Product): how many customers affected? Can we list tenants with requests routed off-region in the last 2 hours? We need to decide whether to throttle fallback or surface a clearer error to customers.
Lee (Support): reported customer count = 4 orgs so far, three reported latency and one reported auth failures. James can share more logs if needed.
billing-bot: Automated Notice: unusual usage spike detected for tenant "acme-corp" between 07:00-07:20 UTC. Estimated spend +32%.
James (Customer): attaching minimal repro curl. We sent region header and auth for eu-west but got redirected and a 503:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_eu_XXXX" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","prompt":"hi"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.example
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> X-Redwood-Region: eu-west
> Authorization: Bearer sk_live_eu_XXXX
< HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect
< Location: https://us-east.api.redwood.example/v1/generate
* Follow-up: redirected to us-east
< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"upstream overloaded"}
```
Tom (Oncall): thanks James. Two actionable things: (1) provide temporary guidance to customers to pin to Dedicated or add region-bearing pins in the request; (2) short-term mitigation: change router fallback to return 409/429 when token scope != target region instead of forwarding. I'll make a config patch now to turn that on as a kill-switch.
Anya (Eng Runtime): I can push a small fix that validates token scope before proxying. Will open PR with tests. ETA ~2h to land in canary. Also adding a metric for "forwarded_with_mismatched_scope".
Karina (SRE): in parallel I'll add a monitoring alert for queue-length-per-pool > 80% and autospill events so we get paging before customer impact. Also collecting traces for other req_ids: req_0d4e5f, req_0f9a2b.
Maria (Product): good. For affected customers we should offer a mitigation note: set header `X-Prefer-Local: true` (server will return 409 when local capacity exhausted) or use pinning via the Console. Can solution docs team draft a short KB? @lee please coordinate.
Lee (Support): will draft KB and DM James with pinning steps.
James (Customer): appreciate it. For now we'll add header to retry logic. Curious if this causes retries to amplify queueing?
Anya (Eng Runtime): yes retries could amplify. We'll recommend exponential backoff and honoring Retry-After headers. Also plan to add a 1-minute soft-throttle for autospill to give queue time to clear.
Tom (Oncall): created internal incident I-2026-347 (priority P2). Assigning to Anya/Karina. Next updates in 30m or on major change.
Karina (SRE): command to pull current router queue snapshot: `kubectl exec -n prod svc/router -- curl -s localhost:9000/queues` sample output:
```
{"eu-west":{"in_flight":320,"queued":112,"capacity":420},"us-east":{"in_flight":210,"queued":20,"capacity":600}}
```
Karina (SRE): I'm also seeing spike in model load times in eu-west, likely caused by many small cold-starts during surge. Suggest pre-warming hotshard pool.
Lee (Support): I'll keep the thread updated and notify customers about the mitigation steps. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Anya (Eng Runtime): PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/834 - adds token-scope precheck + metric. Rolling to canary in ~30m.
Tom (Oncall): once canary looks good we'll flip the fallback-behavior flag. If anyone sees additional orgs affected paste req_ids here.
James (Customer): saw two more req ids: req_0x3c9 and req_0a7b. Happy to share logs privately.
Lee (Support): accepted, created support sub-ticket and linked to incident. Closing loop once patch is deployed and we confirm no further off-region routing for eu-scoped keys.
